title: 二项式反演与斯特林反演

text: At least ⇒ exactly; forced pairs DP.

Binomial inversion (二项式反演): if f(k) = Σi≥k C(i, k) g(i) for all k ("f counts objects with at least k marked items, each counted once per chosen k-subset"), then g(k) = Σi≥k (−1)i−k C(i, k) f(i) ("exactly k").
The other form: f(n) = Σi≤n C(n, i) g(i) ⇔ g(n) = Σi≤n (−1)n−i C(n, i) f(i).

"Exactly k" is hard, "at least k" is easy: choose k items to force the property, arrange the rest freely. Derangements are the case k = 0. 已经没有什么好害怕的了(P4859): count pairings with exactly (n + k)/2 pairs where the candy beats the pill: DP the forced pairs, multiply by (n − j)! for the rest, then invert.

Stirling inversion (斯特林反演) is the analogue with Stirling numbers: f(n) = Σ S(n, k) g(k) ⇔ g(n) = Σ (−1)n−k s(n, k) f(k), where S and s are Stirling numbers of the second and (unsigned) first kind (进阶篇第20章). It converts between "partitions into any number of blocks" and "exactly k blocks".
E[max] from E[min] over subsets; SOS.

Min-max inclusion-exclusion (min-max 容斥): for any finite set S of numbers, max(S) = Σ∅≠T⊆S (−1)|T|+1 min(T). It also holds for expectations, E[max] = Σ (−1)|T|+1 E[min(T)], even though max and min of random variables are not linear. The point: E[min] is often easy when E[max] is not.

按位或(P3175): each second a random number i (probability pi) is ORed into x; expected time until all n bits are set. Tb = time bit b first appears; the answer is E[max Tb]. min over a bit set T is the first time any bit of T appears: geometric with success probability 1 − Σi ∩ T = ∅ pi, i.e. 1 − (sum of p over subsets of T's complement), which SOS DP (拓展篇第12章) gives for all T at once.
Checked against solving the Markov chain over all 2ⁿ states with exact fractions in Python. If some bit can never be set, every T containing it has a zero success probability: the answer is INF.
